title: Rigatoni con polpettine
subtitle: Rigatoni with tiny Italian meatballs in tomato sauce
excerpt: Rigatoni con polpettine pairs thick-ridged pasta tubes with miniature pork-and-beef meatballs simmered in a simple tomato sauce. The meatballs are small enough to slip inside the rigatoni or cling in the ridges. This is Italian home cooking at its most direct: it takes about an hour and feeds a table with minimum fuss.
sourceNotes: Italian-American and southern Italian home-cooking tradition. Small meatball-and-pasta combinations are common across Campania and Calabria. Methods drawn from Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking (1992).

recipe.freezeNotes: The meatballs in tomato sauce freeze well. Thaw overnight and reheat gently before tossing with freshly cooked pasta.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the meatball and sauce quantity and freeze half.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The meatball sauce can be made up to two days ahead and kept in the fridge.

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian diminutive of polpette (meatballs); polpettine are small, typically walnut-sized, designed to pair with pasta rather than to be eaten on their own.

content.text: is a straightforward pasta dish: small meatballs rolled to walnut size, browned in a little oil, then finished in a simple tomato sauce while the pasta boils alongside. The meatballs are soft and seasoned plainly; the tomato sauce does the heavy lifting. This one is popular with children and adults alike.

items.prepNote: good-quality whole peeled, crushed by hand

content.text: Combine {{beef-mince}} of beef mince, {{pork-mince}} of pork mince, the egg, breadcrumbs, Parmesan, parsley, and grated garlic in a bowl with a good pinch of salt. Mix until just combined. Roll into balls roughly the size of large marbles, about 2 cm across. You should get 40 to 50.

Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the meatballs in two batches, turning every minute, until golden all over, about 5 minutes per batch. Transfer to a plate.

In the same pan, cook the onion over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the sliced garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the crushed tomatoes and the passata. Season with salt. Bring to a simmer and add the browned meatballs. Cover loosely and cook for 20 minutes, turning the meatballs once halfway. Add basil at the end if using.
Boil {{pasta-dried}} of rigatoni in well-salted water until al dente. Drain and toss with some of the tomato sauce. Serve topped with the meatballs and more sauce, with Parmesan at the table.

items.symptom: Meatballs fall apart in the pan
items.cause: Not enough binder or mixture was too wet.
items.fix: Add another tablespoon of breadcrumbs and let the mixture rest in the fridge for 15 minutes before rolling. Don't overwork the meat.
Mix until just combined. Over-mixing develops the proteins and makes the meatballs rubbery.
Add a pinch of sugar or a small knob of butter at the end to balance the acidity.

content.text: Small meatballs in tomato sauce are found across southern Italy, mainly in Campania and Calabria. The pasta version, with rigatoni or paccheri, is a Sunday dish in Naples. In Italian-American cooking, the same preparation became spaghetti and meatballs, with larger meatballs and a richer sauce. The Italian original is lighter and simpler.
